summary: Karl Schönfeld was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the universities of Neuchâtel, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and Zurich under Adolf Kaegi, earning a Ph.D. He taught at Kantonsschule Rychenberg from 1905 to 1928.

Indologist and linguist Karl Scriba studied at the University of Munich, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Würzburg, where he completed his PhD around 1900–1902 under doctoral supervisor Julius Jolly.

Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, under August Leskien, and at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He served as a librarian in Halle (1876–1882/1883) and became Docent at Copenhagen in 1882.

Karl Vilhelm Zetterstéen was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his Ph.D. at Uppsala University, studying under Herman Almkvist and Eduard Sachau. He served as docent at Lund (1895–1904) and Professor of Oriental Studies at Uppsala (1904–1931).
Historian Karl von Hegel held academic posts at the University of Rostock from around 1841 to 1856 and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from around 1856 to 1893.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augsburg and Munich (PhD c. 1981). He held posts at the University of Munich, Munich School of Politics and Public Policy, and as professor at FH Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn and his habilitation from the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as the main pupil of Anagarika Govinda from around 1952 to 1985 and succeeded him in 1982.

Karl-Stéphan Bouthillette works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Munich, Laval University, FWO/Ghent University, and Manipal Academy of Higher Education, with an assistant professorship at the University of Hong Kong in 2026.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served as professor at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at Hawaiʻi (2023).

Karma Phuntsho works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at monastic institutes and Oxford (D.Phil.), he was mentored by Richard Gombrich, Michael Aris, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held research posts at CNRS and the University of Cambridge.

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He served as abbot of the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He completed studies at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.
Karmen Bašić was an Indologist who studied at the University of Zagreb and served as Executive Director at the Open Society Institute Croatia from around 1992 to 1999.
Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, whom he also taught.

Karthigesu Indrapala is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Jaffna College, the University of Ceylon, and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1962–1965), and later held a post at the University of Tokyo.

Karuna Kusalasaya was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.
